docs.title: Chemical Treatment Optimization
docs.text: Inhibitor dosage optimization for scale, corrosion and paraffin control in production systems.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Chemical Treatment Optimization", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Source: Synthetic data generator (data_generator.py)
  • Samples: 2,000 treatment records
  • Treatment types: scale_inhibitor, corrosion_inhibitor, demulsifier, paraffin_inhibitor
  • Features: treatment_type, temperature_c, ph, water_hardness, dosage_ppm
  • Targets: dosage_ppm (regression), effectiveness_category (classification)

docs.title: Dosage Optimizer
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoostingRegressor
  • Task: Predict optimal chemical dosage (ppm)
  • Input: treatment_type, temperature_c, ph, water_hardness
  • Output: Optimal dosage in ppm
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Effectiveness Predictor
docs.text:
• Algorithm: RandomForestClassifier
  • Task: Classify treatment effectiveness
  • Input: dosage_ppm, temperature_c, ph, water_hardness, treatment_type
  • Output: Effectiveness category (poor/fair/good/excellent)
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Categorical treatment_type encoded via OneHotEncoder
  2. Numeric features scaled with StandardScaler
  3. Combined feature vector passed to model

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Port: 5009
  • Format: JSON request/response
  • Endpoints: 6 (optimize, predict, health, models, docs, index)

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JS (Jinja2 templates)
  • Charts: Chart.js for visualization
  • Theme: Dark theme UI

docs.title: Dosage Optimization Flow
docs.text:
1. User provides treatment_type + conditions
  2. API validates input and treatment type
  3. GradientBoosting model predicts optimal dosage
  4. Response returned with dosage and echoed conditions

docs.title: Effectiveness Prediction Flow
docs.text:
1. User provides treatment_type + dosage + conditions
  2. API validates input
  3. RandomForest model classifies effectiveness
  4. Response returned with effectiveness category

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.9-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5009

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t chemical-treatment-optimization .
docker run -p 5009:5009 chemical-treatment-optimization

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  chemical-treatment-optimization:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5009:5009"
    environment:
      - FLASK_ENV=production
    volumes:
      - model-data:/app/outputs

volumes:
  model-data:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_ENV Flask environment mode development PORT Server port 5009

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn for production serving: bash gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5009 app:app
  • Set debug=False in app.py (already set)
  • Configure reverse proxy (nginx) for SSL termination
  • Set up health check monitoring on /api/health
  • Use a process manager (systemd, supervisor) for auto-restart

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. python train.py generates synthetic data and trains models
  2. Models are saved to outputs/models/
  3. python app.py loads models and starts the API server

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml): - Runs on push to main - Installs dependencies - Runs training pipeline - Executes API tests

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Chemical Treatment Optimization system uses machine learning to optimize oilfield chemical treatments including scale inhibitors, corrosion inhibitors, demulsifiers, and paraffin inhibitors. It predicts optimal dosages and classifies treatment effectiveness.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd chemical-treatment-optimization
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

This generates 2,000 synthetic samples and trains: - Dosage Optimizer (GradientBoostingRegressor) - Effectiveness Predictor (RandomForestClassifier)

docs.title: Run the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5009 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Dosage Optimization Panel - Enter treatment conditions and get optimal dosage (ppm)
  • Effectiveness Prediction Panel - Enter dosage and conditions to predict treatment effectiveness
  • Chart.js Visualizations - Visual breakdown of treatment parameters
  • Dark Theme UI - Modern dark-themed dashboard

docs.title: Optimize Dosage (curl)
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5009/api/optimize \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "treatment_type": "scale_inhibitor",
    "temperature_c": 65,
    "ph": 7.2,
    "water_hardness": 350
  }'

docs.title: Optimize Dosage (Python)
docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.post("http://localhost:5009/api/optimize", json={
    "treatment_type": "scale_inhibitor",
    "temperature_c": 65,
    "ph": 7.2,
    "water_hardness": 350
})
result = response.json()
print(f"Optimal dosage: {result['optimal_dosage_ppm']} ppm")

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Invalid treatment_type error: Use one of: scale_inhibitor, corrosion_inhibitor, demulsifier, paraffin_inhibitor
  • Models not loaded: Run python train.py first
  • Port in use: Change port in app.py

Elaborado por Ing. Kelvin Cabrera

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
